outcome: Commodity threats are filtered out before they connect, and a stolen password alone no longer opens a way into company systems.
overview: A growing software company usually reaches a point where it has no perimeter worth defending and no security team to run one. Umbrella and Duo are a deliberate pairing for that situation: DNS-layer filtering blocks a large share of commodity threats before a connection is made, and multi-factor authentication with device health closes the account-takeover path that phishing actually uses. Neither is a comprehensive control, and the pairing is chosen precisely because it delivers a disproportionate share of the available risk reduction for very little operational load.

benefits.text: A large share of commodity threats is blocked at DNS resolution, before any connection is made
benefits.limits: DNS-layer filtering is evaded by direct-to-IP connections and by resolvers that bypass the service; it is a broad first filter, not a boundary

benefits.text: Account takeover through stolen credentials is closed by a second factor with device health
benefits.limits: Push-based factors remain vulnerable to fatigue attacks; the design should prefer number matching or a phishing-resistant factor where the application supports it

benefits.text: Both controls are operable by a team with no dedicated security staff
benefits.limits: Low operational load is genuine, and it is also why these controls are sometimes treated as sufficient when they are a starting point

residency: Both are cloud-delivered; DNS query logs and authentication records are held in vendor-operated regions and the tenant region is recorded at design

notFor.situation: An organisation with a secure web gateway and an identity platform already in place
notFor.why: Both capabilities are already covered, more completely, by what exists

notFor.situation: A buyer expecting these two controls to constitute a security programme
notFor.why: They cover two common attack paths well and say nothing about endpoints, data or detection

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco implementation partner · Duration: 3–5 weeks to both controls enforced across the defined population
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. No managed service is proposed, because these controls do not require one.
1) Inventory — applications, user population, current resolver configuration and device management state
2) Design — filtering policy, factor choice per application and the stated coverage boundary
3) Deploy — resolver redirection and roaming client, second factor enrolled per application
4) Measure and hand over — coverage measured, gap statement delivered, operations handed over
deliverables: A managed device off the corporate network resolves through the filtering service, verified by test
Every in-scope application requires the second factor, with the factor type recorded
The handover states explicitly which attack paths remain uncovered
effort: 3–5 weeks to both controls enforced across the defined population
